decisions.reason: Because this 2023 fouling-detection automation disappeared from the website by 2024, management would read it as falling short of aspiration levels and reallocate its resources to stronger core digital-infrastructure projects.

The web tool for weir dimensioning was visible only in its launch year, which suggests weak market pull or limited strategic payoff, so a boundedly rational management would stop carrying it and use the resources elsewhere.
The 2023 fouling-detection system was no longer promoted in 2024, indicating results likely below aspirations and making it sensible to end the offer rather than support overlapping weak products.

As a 2024 launch close to the firm’s established hydraulic-equipment business, this flap weir fits existing capabilities and customers, so an expanding firm with some slack would keep it for another period while learning about demand.

The energy management system is strongly aligned with the firm’s direction toward digitally networked, efficient, and environmentally improved water infrastructure, so management would tolerate early uncertainty and continue backing it.
The overflow flap gate is close to the core offer and was given its own product page, which signals sufficient promise relative to aspirations to keep it on the market.
